## Natural history notes

A small nonnative frog characterized by its brown to reddish-brown body, pointed snout, slender toes, and variable darker markings. In Florida, it is commonly found in moist sheltered habitats such as gardens, greenhouses, leaf litter, mulch, hammocks, yards, and urban or suburban areas. It is mostly active at night and feeds on tiny insects and other small invertebrates, often calling with a soft chirping sound from hidden cover.
